narrative.overview:
G&M Finance is a shared cashbook for two people. The screen should feel like the ledger kept on the kitchen table: exact, unhurried, and out of the way of the numbers. Dark surfaces are the shipped default, so the app stays quiet at night. The blue primary appears only where someone needs to act.

Density is comfortable-to-dense. Small type carries most of the content, many rows fit on one screen, and cards keep generous padding. Hierarchy comes from size and weight, not color. Money is the hero, so amounts are set in tabular figures and colored by direction.

Rejected, confirmed by the user: gradients, glassmorphism, neon accents, a cold and formal bank-portal look, and playful mascots or emoji-heavy copy.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first: the app ships with html class dark
One blue accent; the money-status colors carry direction, not decoration
Flat at rest; shadows only on cards, buttons, and floating layers
Small type with tabular figures on every amount

rules.name: The Direction Rule
rules.body: Green means money in, red means money out, amber means pending or needs attention. These hues never decorate.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount uses tabular-nums so money columns align. Never set an amount in proportional digits.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Rows, list items, and page sections are flat. A shadow means the element can be acted on or floats above the page.

dos: Do use Ledger Blue (primary) for one main action per view.
Do set every amount with tabular-nums and color it by direction: green for in, red for out, Overdraft Red for negative balances.
Do pair color with a word or a sign: Negativo, Em aberto, or a leading minus.
Do keep depth flat at rest. Add shadow only to cards, buttons, and floating layers.
Do keep controls 36px tall with 6px corners, and cards 12px.
donts: Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, or neon accents.
Don't make it look like a cold, formal bank portal, with dense legal-style chrome or intimidating layouts.
Don't use mascots, bright playful gradients, or emoji-heavy copy.
Don't introduce a second accent hue. The blue primary and the three money colors are the palette.
Don't add new gray-* surfaces to screens. Use the tokens and fold drift into them.
Don't use the money-direction colors for decoration.
